heading_ja: 行の調整処理の必要性

cases.quote: Line adjustment processing is applied where inter-character adjustments are needed to bring the line end into the correct alignment, e.g. because of line wrap or other reasons. Within a paragraph, lines are created by separating character sequences at places where line breaking is not prohibited. Except for the end of the last line of a paragraph, it is necessary to set the head and end of each line at predicable, aligned positions. For the last line of the paragraph, it is still necessary to set the head at the aligned position, however the line end need not aligned to the other alignment position. To achieve this, only inter-character spacing indicated in the table of § B. Spacing between Characters , or explicitly chosen spacing, are added, and other inter-character spacing is set solid.
cases.rationale: This case is scoped to text with zero adjustable sites — not because the ladder is unfilled (`crates/jlreq-line/src/lib.rs`'s own `# Status` now states the opposite: `reduce`, `hang` and `expand` are real, and every line `crate::compose` produces "now drains this module rather than reporting `Adjustment::empty` unconditionally", `crate::ladder`'s own `# Status` in full) — but because isolating §3.8.1's own claim from the ladder's own, now-real behavior is the reason to keep this fixture the way it is. Three ideographs (cl-19, no inter-character spacing of their own — Table 1's cl-19-against-cl-19 cell is blank — and the second line's own extent below, 1000, exactly the third character's own advance, shows the line-end boundary carries no term for it either) give both lines this case composes zero `Site`s to drain: `ladder::reduce` and `ladder::hang` run as no-ops on both lines because there is nothing for either to touch. `ladder::expand` is not even called for the second line, because `crate::compose::adjust_line` gates it on `kind.is_none() && !is_last_line` — the same gate `crate::compose`'s own `# Status` ties to §3.8.1's Note, "the last line still takes reduction, never expansion" — and this case verifies that gate directly: were it dropped, `adjust_line` would ask `ladder::expand` to close the second line's own 1000-unit shortfall against a ladder with no sites at all, and `expand`'s own doc states what that returns, "how much of `need` could not be placed (zero unless the ladder has no expandable site at all)", so the line would come back `ExpansionExhausted` rather than the conforming, unstretched 1000-unit extent `permitted` states below. What this fixture does not exercise, by the same zero-site fact, is the ladder's own drain arithmetic — the weighted split across `reduce`'s priority stages, `hang`'s own eligibility check, or `expand`'s ordinary and re-leveled stages — which is exactly right for a case whose own `quote` is §3.8.1's line-fitting claim and not §3.8.2's, §3.8.3's or §3.8.4's: a fixture with a reducible or expandable boundary could fail this case for a bug in `ladder::reduce` or `ladder::expand` rather than for a bug in the last-line exemption or the aligned-position claim §3.8.1 itself states, conflating two different rules under one `permitted`/`forbidden` pair. The ladder's own arithmetic has its own cases instead, each built over a fixture with a real, nonzero shortfall for exactly this reason: `3.8.2.json` (hanging punctuation closing what reduction alone cannot), `3.8.3.json` (the fourth stage's own character-size-weighted split across two sites), and `3.8.4.json` (ordinary second- and third-stage expansion and the fourth stage's own re-leveling). What the rule states beyond the ladder is observable here regardless: a non-last line reaches the measure exactly, because that is what "predictable, aligned positions" at both ends means, while the last line reaches it at the head and stops wherever its own content ends, because "the line end need not [be] aligned to the other alignment position." On a two-em measure the same three ideographs force exactly two lines: the first two characters fill the first line to precisely 2000 units with nothing added or removed, and the third sits alone on the second line at 1000 units, a thousand short of the measure and left that way — not stretched, not flagged, because line adjustment already achieved what §3.8.1 asks of it: the last line's head is aligned and its end is not, and no character-spacing adjustment ran because none was owed by either line, and none was available for the ladder to run regardless.

forbidden.why: §3.8.1 excuses only the last line's own line end from reaching the aligned position; stretching its content to the full measure anyway answers a rule that requires every line's end to align, which is the rule's own first sentence about every line but the last, not this one.
